problem: Real browser attempts failed when the base field helper emitted a thought prefix before JSON. This prototype constrains generated syntax while leaving field values unrestricted.
language: Exactly one decoded text key with a Unicode scalar string or null; JSON whitespace and escapes allowed, paired surrogates required. Extra keys, fences and thought prefixes refuse.
decoder: Preserves Replace then ByteFallback then Fuse semantics. A fallback byte run retains valid and replacement projections until it ends; a later invalid byte can replace the entire run.
limits: The existing helper and qualified service are unchanged. This is neither a live latency result nor a field-value correctness result. Null, blank and oversized values still require the existing consumer refusal; reaching128 tokens does not justify appending EOS or repairing output.
next: Integrate through a separately reviewed helper adapter and fresh runtime qualification, then test real browser tasks.
